arxiv-2012-12168.title: Hahn polynomials for hypergeometric distribution Thanks: The first author is partially supported by Simons Foundation Grant #635462.
arxiv-2012-12168.creator: Plamen Iliev, Yuan Xu
arxiv-2012-12168.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Plamen Iliev, Yuan Xu. Orthogonal polynomials for the multivariate hypergeometric distribution are defined on lattices in polyhedral domains in ℝ d {\mathbb{R}}^{d} . Their structures are studied through a detailed analysis of classical Hahn polynomials with negative integer parameters. Factorization of the Hahn polynomials is explored and used to explain the relation between the index set of orthogonal polynomials and the lattice set in polyhedral domain. In the multivariate case, these constructions lead to nontrivial families of hypergeometric polynomials vanishing on lattice polyhedra.

arxiv-2112-04063.title: Semantic OcTree Mapping and Shannon Mutual Information Computation for Robot Exploration
arxiv-2112-04063.creator: Arash Asgharivaskasi, Nikolay Atanasov
arxiv-2112-04063.description: Abstract Autonomous robot operation in unstructured and unknown environments requires efficient techniques for mapping and exploration using streaming range and visual observations. Information-based exploration techniques, such as Cauchy-Schwarz quadratic mutual information (CSQMI) and fast Shannon mutual information (FSMI), have successfully achieved active binary occupancy mapping with range measurements.

arxiv-2206-08311.title: Continuous-Time Modeling of Counterfactual Outcomes Using Neural Controlled Differential Equations
arxiv-2206-08311.creator: Nabeel Seedat, Fergus Imrie, Alexis Bellot, Zhaozhi Qian, Mihaela van der Schaar
arxiv-2206-08311.description: Abstract Estimating counterfactual outcomes over time has the potential to unlock personalized healthcare by assisting decision-makers to answer “what-if” questions. Existing causal inference approaches typically consider regular, discrete-time intervals between observations and treatment decisions and hence are unable to naturally model irregularly sampled data, which is the common setting in practice.

arxiv-2410-09610.title: The onset of filamentation on vorticity interfaces in two-dimensional Euler flows
arxiv-2410-09610.creator: David G. Dritschel 1, Adrian Constantin 2, Pierre M. Germain 3
arxiv-2410-09610.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by David G. Dritschel 1, Adrian Constantin 2, Pierre M. Germain 3. Two-dimensional Euler flows, in the plane or on simple surfaces, possess a material invariant, namely the scalar vorticity normal to the surface. Consequently, flows with piecewise-uniform vorticity remain that way, and moreover evolve in a way which is entirely determined by the instantaneous shapes of the contours (interfaces) separating different regions of vorticity — this is known as ‘Contour Dynamics’.

arxiv-2505-10981.title: Rethinking the Role of Prompting Strategies in LLM Test-Time Scaling: A Perspective of Probability Theory
arxiv-2505-10981.creator: Yexiang Liu, Zekun Li, Zhi Fang, Nan Xu, Ran He, Tieniu Tan
arxiv-2505-10981.description: Abstract Recently, scaling test-time compute on Large Language Models (LLM) has garnered wide attention. However, there has been limited investigation of how various reasoning prompting strategies perform as scaling. In this paper, we focus on a standard and realistic scaling setting: majority voting. We systematically conduct experiments on 6 LLMs × \times 8 prompting strategies × \times 6 benchmarks.

pmc-13117005.creator: Guido Gembillo, Luca Soraci, Matteo Floris, Lorenzo Lo Cicero, Claudia Lo Re, Elvira Filicetti, Michela Calderone, Carmelo Giorgio Benenati, Andrea Corsonello, Domenico Santoro

pmc-13177119.description: Acne vulgaris is a common dermatological condition that often affects psychological well-being, with depression, anxiety and reduced quality of life being frequently observed. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 207 patients, assessing psychological status using established tools.
